simple.meaning: בֹּהוּ (bôhûw) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a vacuity , i.e. (superficially) an undistinguishable ruin.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Genesis, Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at Genesis 1:2. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בֹּהוּ (H922).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: בֹּהוּ (bôhûw) / H922 is traced through Genesis 1:2, Isaiah 34:11, Jeremiah 4:23 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: a vacuity , i.e. (superficially) an undistinguishable ruin

firstOccurrence.englishText: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.

timeline.evidenceText: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
But the pelican and the porcupine will possess it.
I saw the earth, and, behold, it was waste and void, and the heavens, and they had no light.

definitions.short: a vacuity , i.e. (superficially) an undistinguishable ruin
definitions.full: H922. bohu בֹּ֫הוּ noun [masculine] emptiness (on form see Ges § 84a , 1 b Sta § 95, 198 a, on usage compare Lag Or. ii. 60 f. ) always with תֹּהוּ q. v.; — וָבֹהוּ תֹּהוּ Gen 1:2 of primeval earth; Jer 4:23 of earth under judgment of ׳י ; בֹהוּ וְאַבְנֵי קַותֿֿהֹוּ Isa 34:11 , the line of wasteness and the stones of emptiness , i.e. plummets, employed, not as usual for building, but for destroying walls; compare Di & see below אבן 6
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root (meaning to be empty);
